newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Word on Olo Brown expected today.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Word on Olo Brown expected today.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Oct 21 - The Auckland Rugby Union (ARU) is expected to make an announcement today on whether All Blacks prop Olo Brown will be fit to play in next Sunday's NPC first division final against Counties, NZPA reports.
Brown was knocked senseless three minutes from the end of Auckland's 59-18 win over Otago by a tremendous shoulder tackle put on him by Otago's Isitolo Maka.
He lay motionless and spreadeagled for more than a minute and was then helped staggering from the field.

While Auckland coach Graham Henry said afterwards that he didn't know if Brown was concussed and that the prop would be put through medical tests this week, he and his manager Rex Davy took the strange step of gagging their doctor Graham Paterson.
Paterson, who has previously discussed the concussion of All Blacks Michael Jones, told NZPA last night that he had been instructed to direct all comment on Brown to Davy or Henry.
While Paterson wouldn't comment, All Blacks doctor John Mayhew told NZPA the international ruling on concussion was quite clear.
"There is a law for concussion and it is the three-week stand down period," Mayhew said.
"If Olo was concussed, as he appeared to be, then it would be unwise to play him next weekend.
"I am sure ultimately Olo's health and safety will be given the greatest consideration."
The issue over Brown's concussion overshadowed an otherwise electrifying Auckland performance in which they scored nine tries.
After leading 19-6 at halftime, Auckland, with first five-eighth Carlos Spencer playing the game of his life in scoring five tries, powered away for a comfortable win.
"Maybe only food poisoning will stop them," Otago captain Taine Randell joked after the match.
"I felt they almost took the throttle off against us at times."
Both he and his coach Glenn Ross could only marvel at the brilliance of Spencer who scored two long range tries including a sensational piece of cheek.
When Spencer moved to score his second try, he held out the ball, showing it to Otago fullback Jeff Wilson, then just as suddenly he flashed a dummy, sidestepped Wilson and took off to score.
"Carlos Spencer is an extremely talented player with marvellous allround skill, great composure and temperament," Ross said.
Henry, who was at Pukekohe yesterday to watch Counties put Canterbury away 46-33, said his side won't be resting until the final ambition for the season is realised.
"There are goals we are trying to achieve, we wanted three titles for the season (Super 12, Ranfurly Shield, NPC) and to win the NPC four times in a row."
Auckland are firm favourites to win at Eden Park next Sunday, even without Jones and possibly Brown.
